description: Control structures on the Lower Lea for the c.1895 flood model (FLOOD_MODEL_PLAN.md, Phase 0 draft for the author's review, 5 October 2026). One record per mill, lock, weir, flood gate and sluice the OS five-foot plan shows or the sources document. Every number is marked documented, mapped, estimate or unknown, with its method and the readings that bound it. Nothing reads this file yet.
frame: scene x = easting - 538900, z = 183209 - northing; levels are scene y metres; odnMetres = sceneY + 1.83544 (data/maps/os-tide-levels.json datum)
status: draft, revised after the author's Phase 0 review (5 October 2026); back-river beds (decision 4) still open

decisions: Pudding Mill held water; City Mills still operational to some extent; no mill on the Waterworks River in the 1890s
Model working mills as tide-mill ponds held at the last high water (plan 4.2 changed)
The Navigation and the Three Mills pond are kept apart by a wall/bank; the Navigation held its level and let the river through to Bow Creek (confirmed on the maps: the Three Mills overfall)
Several flood types eventually; the flood from rain up river first

structures.name: Three Mills (House Mill 1776, Clock Mill 1817)

crossLine.status: approximate, read on the crop: the mill range between the pond (Three Mills Wall and Back Rivers) and the race to Bow Creek

pond.note: The pond is the water above the mill: the Three Mills Wall and Back Rivers, up the back rivers (3, 7, 9) to the Stratford mills. It is walled off from the Navigation: from Bow Bridge to Three Mills the Bow Bridge Works strip and the island above the mill lie between them (1860s and 1893 plans). The Navigation spills into it over the Three Mills overfall, and the Bow Back River joins the two through the Marshgate Lane lock.

structures.mechanism: The flood tide entered the pond through one-way gates and the gates closed as the tide turned; the ebb was then run through the wheels (book ch. 1, PDF p. 46, describing the medieval tide mills). The 1930s Prescott sluice was built so that the tide-driven wheels could run longer (Bow Locks page), so the wheels were still tide-driven after 1900.

pondFullSceneY.method: The pond fills to the high water of the tide that fills it: ordinary tides 1.578 (Trinity High Water). Neaps fill it less, springs and surges more.

pondDrawdownFloorSceneY.method: The lowest pond level at the end of milling, set by the race sills and the wheels. No sill is surveyed. Bounded below by the 1908 canal standard bed (six feet below the Bow overshot level, about -0.9; book p. 200), which the engineers proposed as a deepening, so the silted beds stood above it; the back rivers were navigable only at spring tides (book p. 200), which also puts the beds high.

raceSillSceneY.method: Not surveyed; the House Mill Trust may hold a record of the race floors.

openingWidthMetres.method: Wheel bays and race at the House Mill and Clock Mill, read as about 8 m of effective width (4 to 12). The model's House Mill race passage is 3 m wide for display only (task D).

dischargeCoefficient.method: Sluice/orifice coefficient for flow under gates; generic engineering value.

operatingStates: working (fill on the flood, hold, run on the ebb)
shut (held; no milling, no tide entry)

evidence: VCH Essex vi pp. 89-93: J. & W. Nicholson, gin distillers, owned the mills from 1872; distilling ceased 1941; water-powered machinery survives in the House Mill and Clock Mill
book ch. 6 p. 202: in 1908 the owners would not give up the mills for flood defence
book ch. 1 p. 67: the millers' long-standing rights to the tidal flow limited the LCB and the borough

existence.1809: present; the eighteenth-century embankment that trapped more tide for Three Mills and Four Mills was the subject of the 1824-30 dispute (book ch. 1 p. 49)
existence.1928: present (fires 1908 and 1920 destroyed other buildings, VCH)

structures.name: Abbey Mill (Corn)

crossLine.status: approximate, read on the crop: across both passages beside the mill (the mill stood on an island in the Channelsea, VCH)

structures.mechanism: The OS letters "Highest Point to which the O.T. flow" here (task C). The upper Channelsea's banks and streets stand below ordinary high water, so the mill's gates must have kept the tide out and let the river out at low water: a head held against the tide, not a tide mill pond.

retainedSceneY.method: The upper Channelsea's ordinary level. It must lie below the lowest readings along it with room to spare, and the model now holds it at 0.06 (illustrative).

gateTopSceneY.method: At least ordinary high water, since ordinary tides stopped here; below the B.M. on the mill (2.785) and Abbey Road at the tidal-limit note (2.188).

openingWidthMetres.method: Two passages either side of the mill island, about 4 and 6 m on the five-foot plan (read on the crop, +/- 2 m each).

operatingStates: working (tide gates shut against the flood; head held; river released at low water)
gates drawn (open; the tide runs up the Channelsea)

evidence: VCH: let to William and James Hunt in 1881, family tenants until about 1936; ceased to operate by 1929; rebuilt 1863-4

structures.name: Bow overshoot (stepped overfall beside the Tidal Lock)

crossLine.status: mapped extent of the stepped masonry hatching on the five-foot plan; read on the crop

structures.interpretation: The OS draws a long stepped masonry structure between the Navigation and Bow Creek beside the lock. Read here as an overfall that, with the Three Mills overfall, sets the Navigation's normal head; the book's 1892/1908 canal standard is measured from "the overshot level at Bow Lock" (p. 200). The 1852 "western flood gate" (Bow Locks page) has not been located and may be part of it.

structures.name: Three Mills overfall (the "Three Mills Overshoot")

crossLine.status: mapped: lettered "Overfall" on the 1860s 1:1,056 plan at the head of the island above Three Mills; a short link with a footbridge (F.B.) on the 1893 plan

structures.mechanism: Spills the Navigation into the Three Mills pond. With the Bow overshoot it holds the Navigation at its normal head; the surplus river runs through the pond and Three Mills to Bow Creek (the author's reading, 5 October 2026). The 1898 proposal for a lock or tide gate "at the junction of the 3 Mills Back River and the Navigation, near the Three Mills Overshoot" was turned down (Bow Locks page). At high tide the pond rises above the head and the overfall runs backwards.

structures.name: City Mills (Spilemans) and flood gates

crossLine.status: approximate: the City Mill River passes under the City Mills (Chemical) buildings; passages not resolved

structures.mechanism: An ancient tide mill north of the High Street. Ordinary tides reached Temple Mills (OS note), so the flood passed the Stratford mills. The City of London owned the mills and their flood gates on the City Mill and Waterworks Rivers, in disrepair by 1920.

heldHeadSceneY.method: If working as a tide mill: the high water of the tide, as at Three Mills.

openingWidthMetres.method: Passage under the buildings, read on the crop; uncertain.

evidence: author, 5 October 2026: still operational to some extent
os-london-town-plan-1860s and os-london-five-foot-1893: the mill spans the City Mill River at the footbridge
VCH: Howard & Allen (Howards & Sons, manufacturing chemists) leased part from 1805 and gradually took the whole site, until 1914; corn-grinding last recorded 1818
book ch. 6 p. 205: City Mill and Waterworks floodgates in disrepair in 1920

existence.1809: working mill (corn; Howard & Allen chemists in part from 1805)

structures.name: Waterworks River flood gate

crossLine.status: approximate: the OS "Flood Gate" at a narrow passage with a footbridge (F.B.)

structures.mechanism: On the site of the old Waterworks (Saynes) Mill: the 1848-51 skeleton survey draws buildings across the river here, and the 1893 plan a Flood Gate with a footbridge (the 1848 layer is registered only approximately). No mill by 1893-4 (VCH; the author agrees). The river above runs between hatched banks. Read as one of the City's flood gates (book p. 205), shut against high tides or drawn to pass floods; its use is not recorded.

gateTopSceneY.method: Not surveyed; nearby streets 14.3-14.5 ft (2.13-2.19 m).

openingWidthMetres.method: Passage width read on the crop.

structures.name: Waterworks Mill (Saynes Mill)
structures.mechanism: VCH: occupied by factories 1873-81 and gone by 1893-4. Its site is the 1893 Flood Gate (waterworks-flood-gate). No mill in the 1890s model; it matters for the 1809 model.

existence.1809: working (West Ham Waterworks Co. rebuilt the corn-mill and added a pumping engine by 1775)

structures.name: St Thomas's Mills (Pudding Mill; Du Barry's Patent Food)

crossLine.status: approximate: the only passage, through the mill (author)

structures.mechanism: The river runs only through the mill: St Thomas's Mill (Corn) in the 1860s, (Patent Food) in 1893. The head channel above the mill has a hatched embankment on its east side on the 1893 plan, a raised mill head. The author (5 October 2026): Pudding Mill must have held water. Little water came down the Pudding Mill River even in floods by 1908 (book p. 204).

heldHeadSceneY.method: A former tide mill: the pond fills to the high water of the tide, as at Three Mills; the embanked head could hold it. Below the bank and street readings by the mill (16.2 ft, 2.71; 16.5 ft, 2.80).

drawdownFloorSceneY.method: Higher than at Three Mills: a small, silted, embanked head.

openingWidthMetres.method: Narrow through-mill passage; read on the crop.

evidence: os-london-town-plan-1860s: St Thomas's Mill (Corn) across the river
VCH: Du Barry & Co. (flour miller, later patent food) lessee 1864, owner 1875, until about 1925

structures.name: Lock on the Bow Back River west of Marshgate Lane
structures.mechanism: The Bow Back River runs from an open mouth on the Navigation near Bow Bridge to this lock; east of the lock are the back rivers (the Three Mills pond). The lock kept the Navigation's head apart from the tidal back rivers. The Bow Back River is not on the 1860s plan: it was cut between the 1860s and 1893.

existence.1860s: absent (no Bow Back River on the 1:1,056 plan)

structures.name: Four Mills (Bromley)
structures.mechanism: Historically the Four Mills held the Lea behind Bow Lock (sill raised in the 1660s; 1711 penning complaints; the 1824 dispute over the embankment). By 1893-96 the site is the Four Mills Distillery and Sun Mills (Corn), with the tidal "Mud" basin; no dam is drawn. Kept for the 1809 model.

flowEvidence.source: G2G_Oudin_flow_1891_2015.csv (author, untracked), column 38001 (Lee at Feildes Weir), modelled daily means
flowEvidence.parsingNote: Dates are ISO to 1899 and dd/mm/yyyy from 1900. The plan's figures (median 4.6, Q95 2.0, peak 40.9 on 15 Nov 1894) cover 1891-1899 only.
flowEvidence.caution: Modelled natural flow. In dry summers the waterworks took most of the Lea (book p. 66; the 1860s commissioners, p. 79), so far less reached the back rivers than G2G gives. Daily means, not event peaks.
